question: Is physical activity associated with diabetes?
refined_question: Among noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic (Age >=18 years; excluding pregnant at examination), is any vigorous recreational activity associated with a higher prevalence of diabetes - self-report, medication, or HbA1c >=6.5%, after adjustment for age, sex, race and ethnicity, income-to-poverty ratio, educational attainment, smoking status, and body mass index?
title: Association of Physical Activity With Diabetes Among US Adults: NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic
hypothesis: Any vigorous recreational activity is associated with a higher prevalence of diabetes - self-report, medication, or HbA1c >=6.5%.

pico.population: noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic (Age >=18 years; excluding pregnant at examination)
pico.covariates: Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Educational attainment, Smoking status, and Body mass index

model.rationale: Binary outcome: survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression with log link estimates prevalence ratios (PRs). PRs are preferred to odds ratios for cross-sectional data because ORs exaggerate associations when the outcome is common (>10%); the quasi-Poisson variance is robust under the design-based (Taylor linearization) estimator. Logistic regression is run as a sensitivity analysis.

adjustment_sets.label: Adjusted for age, sex, and race and ethnicity

missing_data.rationale: Complete-case primary analysis within the design; multiple imputation by chained equations as sensitivity analysis when covariates are missing.

sensitivity.label: Exclude participants aware of the diagnosis (reverse causation)

rationale.statistician: Binary outcome: survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression with log link estimates prevalence ratios (PRs). PRs are preferred to odds ratios for cross-sectional data because ORs exaggerate associations when the outcome is common (>10%); the quasi-Poisson variance is robust under the design-based (Taylor linearization) estimator. Logistic regression is run as a sensitivity analysis.
rationale.epidemiologist: Covariates were selected as plausible common causes of any vigorous recreational activity and diabetes - self-report, medication, or HbA1c >=6.5% (minimal confounder set from the domain library): Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Educational attainment, Smoking status, and Body mass index. Variables on the causal pathway or sharing laboratory components with the outcome/exposure are excluded to avoid over-adjustment.

limitations: Cross-sectional design: temporality cannot be established and associations must not be interpreted causally.
Single measurement of laboratory values; within-person variability and chronicity cannot be assessed.
Residual confounding by unmeasured or imperfectly measured factors (e.g., diet, medications, menstrual blood loss).
Self-reported comorbidities and behaviours are subject to recall and social-desirability bias.
NHANES excludes institutionalized and active-duty military populations.
Operational definition (ADA (HbA1c)): Fasting glucose omitted so the full MEC sample/weight can be used; add FPG >=126 mg/dL in a fasting-subsample sensitivity analysis.

variable_map.expr: cases(RIDRETH3 == 3, "Non-Hispanic White", RIDRETH3 == 4, "Non-Hispanic Black", RIDRETH3 %in% c(1, 2), "Hispanic", RIDRETH3 == 6, "Non-Hispanic Asian", RIDRETH3 == 7, "Other or multiracial")

variable_map.expr: cases(DMDEDUC2 %in% c(1, 2), "Less than high school", DMDEDUC2 == 3, "High school or GED", DMDEDUC2 == 4, "Some college", DMDEDUC2 == 5, "College graduate or above")

checks.title: Outcome is partly defined by treatment
checks.detail: Treated people count as cases. If the exposure affects access to care, outcome misclassification will differ by exposure. Report the measured-only definition as a sensitivity analysis.

checks.title: Run the PubMed/MEDLINE novelty check
checks.detail: A stated hypothesis exists; checking prior NHANES work documents the a priori rationale and avoids re-running a crowded exposure-outcome pair.

checks.title: Approve to hash-lock the protocol before results
checks.detail: SHA-256 of the analysis plan is recorded at approval; any later edit voids the approval. All 6 prespecified sensitivity analyses are reported regardless of result; 5 subgroup/interaction tests are labelled exploratory.

checks.title: Add a named statistician or epidemiologist sign-off
checks.detail: Investigator approval is required to run; journals increasingly expect documented methodological co-authorship for large-database studies.

checks.title: Explicit, same-population comparator
checks.detail: Contrast: participants in the same eligible population without any vigorous recreational activity. Both groups come from the same probability sample and eligibility criteria (no convenience controls).

checks.title: Outcome includes measured (exam or laboratory) data
checks.detail: Objective measurement captures undiagnosed cases, unlike code-based EHR outcomes.

checks.title: Reverse causation: diagnosed people may have changed behaviour
checks.detail: People who know their diagnosis often change diet, activity or smoking (sick-quitter effect), which can reverse the apparent association. Sensitivity analysis excluding diagnosed participants is planned.

checks.title: Prespecified adjustment set
checks.detail: Adjusted for 7 covariates. Mediators and definitional overlaps are removed automatically, and an E-value quantifies how strong unmeasured confounding would need to be.

checks.title: Executable methods with data provenance
checks.detail: Every result comes with the compiled plan, R code, reproduce.R and MD5 checksums of the exact CDC files - the methods section describes what actually ran.
checks.critique: Methods the platform cannot actually run

design_audit.framework: Criticisms of EHR-network (TriNetX-style) studies: comparator, outcome, temporality, confounding, rationale, prespecification, reproducibility, meaningfulness, oversight.

review.title: Multiplicity
review.detail: Many subgroup/interaction tests - interpret as exploratory or adjust for multiple comparisons.
